# CANDIDATE: MIDDAY_GAP_FADE_50RET

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When the opening gap remains unfilled by midday (11:00 ET), a 50% retracement of the gap often precedes a full fill, offering a fade opportunity. This edge exists because gaps that are not filled early in the day may indicate underlying pressure in the opposite direction, and the 50% retracement level acts as a magnet for price before the gap is filled.

## Mechanism

Entry rule: Define gap size = open - prior close (positive for gap up, negative for gap down). If at 11:00 ET the price has not retraced more than 30% of the gap size, wait until price retraces exactly 50% of the gap (i.e., price = prior close + 0.5*gap size) on a closing basis; enter in the direction of gap fill (short for gap up, long for gap down) on the bar that closes at that level. Exit shape: Stop at the opposite gap edge (i.e., prior close for gap up fade, open for gap down fade); target full gap fill (price = prior close) with a trailing stop of 0.2× ATR after hitting 50% of gap. Regime hint: Effective when VIX > 18 (elevated volatility) and during the period 10:30‑12:00 ET; avoid when VIX < 12 (low volatility) as gaps tend to persist.

5. **Failure modes:** 
   - Worst day: Gap continues in opening direction (gap-and-go) preventing 50% retracement entry or causing late entries
   - Max drawdown: Stop at opposite gap edge may be hit after large adverse move if gap extends then reverses
   - Blow-up scenario: Strong trending day with extending gap triggers multiple fade entries, each stopped out at prior close (now far adverse price), causing series of losses
